title: Test failure diagnosis
description: Why each failure in a captured test run failed, classified into four causes. The producer does not run the suite: running is a script's work and its output is this artifact's input, which keeps the run reproducible independently of the judgment about it. `failures_reported` is required alongside `diagnoses` so that a failure nobody examined cannot hide behind a complete-looking artifact — the two disagreeing is the defect the field exists to expose. The artifact carries no severity and no overall pass or fail: foundation/0005 R5 keeps a specialized agent from choosing what runs next, and ranking failures is a question about the project rather than about a failure.

contract_version.description: A consumer rejects an artifact it was not built to read rather than inferring version from shape.

diagnosis_id.description: Stable identifier for this diagnosis, supplied by the caller and never minted by the producer.

producer.description: What performed the diagnosis. Not a const: the contract requires the artifact, not a particular producer of it.

run_output.description: Path of the captured runner output this diagnosis was computed from. Required: a diagnosis that cannot name its run states a conclusion nobody can re-derive.

failures_reported.description: How many failures the runner reported. `diagnoses` must hold one entry for each. A delegation over a run with no failure is not an error in the run and returns no artifact at all.

diagnoses.description: One entry per reported failure, sorted by file then line.

name.description: The test name as the runner printed it, so an entry resolves against the output rather than against a reading of the source.

cause.description: `code` the implementation is wrong and the expectation is right; `test` the reverse; `setup` neither was reached because the environment prevented a real result; `build` nothing ran. Where no specification statement settles code against test, the value is `code` — the reading that constrains more, because it keeps a wrong implementation from being closed by editing its test.

evidence.description: The runner's own message for this failure, quoted, with expected and received values where the runner printed them. Not the producer's restatement of it.

reason.description: Why this cause and not the neighbouring one. For `code` and `test` this names the specification statement that settles it, or says plainly that none does.

correction.description: What to change, specific enough to act on without re-reading the output. Naming the change is not making it: nothing here is applied by the producer.

notes.description: Anything a reader needs to interpret the result that no other field holds — most often that the change under test was not supplied, so no failure was attributed to an untouched area.
